newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs end firm in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs end firm in quiet trade.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures finished mildly firmer in slow trade on Wednesday, with dealers betting on further gains as both ends of the Japanese yield curve continued to defy gravity.
December and March Euroyen saw turnover of more than 4,000 lots each and ended at 99.42 and 99.34 against their IMM settlements at 99.41 and 99.31 respectively.
Japanese government bond futures for December settled at 123.50 against their opening 123.10.
Eurodollar futures ended slightly firmer as sentiment remained buoyant following last Friday's unexpected decline in U.S. non-farm payrolls for September.

Dealers said the market would scrutinise U.S. wholesale and consumer inflation data, expected later this week and next week, for a confirmation of the view that the U.S. economy was not in danger of overheating.
March Eurodollars ended at 94.31 against their IMM close 94.28.
Dealers said sentiment was likely to remain positive ahead of the Japanese general election on October 20 as market participants had practically ruled out an interest rate hike before next March.
A trader with a U.S. futures house said March Euroyen showed potential to breach its contract high of 99.36 and head towards 99.40 ahead of the elections.
"The spreads have been quite active in recent days," he said, adding that players were buying the front months and selling the back months on expectations of steady rates in the foreseeable future.
